name: promotion_redemptions
title: Promotion Redemptions
description: One row per use of a code, append-only: these rows ARE the redemption count (promotions.redemptions_used is a rollup over them), so a row is never edited or deleted -- a use given back is a compensating record on the order that gave it back, exactly as refunds correct payments and reversing journals correct postings (docs/logic-decisions.md #3). The load-bearing property is that THE TERMS ARE STAMPED HERE: kind, value, minimum_spend_cents and stacking are copied off the promotion at the moment somebody redeems it, so editing the promotion next month changes what the NEXT shopper gets and nothing else. Without that stamp, a shop that raises SPRING20 from 10% to 20% silently restates every receipt already issued under it, and the customer asking why their order shows one number and the promotion page shows another is right to be confused. discount_cents is the money that actually came off, computed once by object_promotions.discount_for and recorded rather than recomputed: a number rederived later from terms that have since moved is the very drift this row exists to prevent. code_used is stored upper-cased -- the comparison form -- because that is what a fold over these rows matches on.

fields.name: code_used
fields.label: Code
fields.help: The code as it was COMPARED -- trimmed and upper-cased. Kept beside the relation on purpose: a promotion row can be retired, and the receipt still has to be able to say which word the customer typed.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: STAMPED: what the promotion was when this was redeemed. Plain text and not an enum, because this is a historical record of a term, and a later narrowing of the promotion's own enum must never make an old redemption unreadable.

fields.name: value
fields.label: Value
fields.help: STAMPED: basis points or cents, whichever the stamped kind meant.

fields.name: minimum_spend_cents
fields.label: Minimum Spend
fields.help: STAMPED: the threshold this redemption was actually judged against, so a later change to the promotion cannot make a past use look like it should have been refused.

fields.name: stacking
fields.label: Stacking
fields.help: STAMPED: whether this code allowed company at the time it was used.

fields.name: order_id
fields.label: Order
fields.help: The sale it came off. This is the join that makes a redemption auditable: what was bought, for how much, and what the code took off it.

fields.name: customer_email
fields.label: Customer
fields.help: Who used it, which is what a per-customer limit counts. Matched case-insensitively, because the same address with a capital letter is the same person.

fields.name: discount_cents
fields.label: Discount
fields.help: The money that actually came off, in cents, computed once at redemption. Recorded rather than recomputed later: a number rederived from terms that have moved is exactly the drift this row exists to prevent.

fields.name: redeemed_at
fields.label: Redeemed
fields.help: When it was used. Stamped by the writer rather than left to created_at so a backfilled or imported redemption can carry its real moment.
